In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of estrogen deficiency and inflammatory cytokines in the development of hypertension and cardiovascular disease in women.

the role of inflammatory cytokines in the pathogenesis of hypertension, the role of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) in modulating inflammatory cytokines, and the role of estrogen deficiency in the pathogenesis and treatment of hypertension.
the effects of estrogen deficiency on vascular inflammation and the potential role of inflammatory cytokines in mediating the vascular dysfunction associated with menopause and aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
estrogen deficiency is not the only risk factor for cardiovascular disease, and that the risk factors for postmenopausal hypertension and cardiovascular disease are multifactorial.

the data are consistent with the hypothesis that estrogen deficiency is associated with an increase in inflammatory cytokine production and that this is associated with an increased incidence of cardiovascular disease.
the data are consistent with the hypothesis that estrogen deficiency increases cardiovascular disease risk by increasing the production of inflammatory mediators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data support the hypothesis that inflammatory cytokines are important mediators of the cardiovascular effects of estrogen deficiency.
we have shown that the loss of ovarian function in women leads to an increase in the production of proinflammatory cytokines.
